messages:
laura.design: quick design review — thinking through a guardrail for canary traffic targeting + the density of the version-history timeline. sketch here: https://img.redwood/mock/canary-guardrail.png. main questions: copy for the speedbump, contrast for the traffic bar, and whether mini-timeline needs to be denser or more readable.
ben_pm: tl;dr — want an extra confirmation when someone pushes >20% to a canary. we had a near-miss last week. :sweat_smile:
mike.eng: fwiw, implementation wise we can do a few levers: slider snap increments (1% under 10%, 5% above), and a threshold modal for >20% that requires typing the variant name. cheap to add.
aria_a11y: contrast note — the traffic heatmap colors currently sit at ~2.8:1 on the mid tones. need >=4.5:1 for the small legend text and 3:1 for large text. also keyboard users need clear focus on the slider thumb and an aria-live update when allocation changes.
sophia_research: from the last 6 sessions people confused "Canary" vs "Variant" labels — suggest “Target: Canary (v2-alpha)” or show a tiny badge. people also misread the mini-timeline when there are >6 versions.
laura.design: thinking microcopy for the modal: keep it calm, action-oriented. proposal: ```You are about to route 50% of production traffic to Canary ‘v2-alpha’. This will increase exposure to new code. Confirm to proceed.``` open to wording suggestions — is "exposure" too alarmist?
ben_pm: maybe swap to: "This will increase user exposure to the new variant and could increase errors." then add an optional checklist: monitoring, rollback plan, alert contacts. also we should log the reason field (free text) so PMs see context later.
mike.eng: +1 on logging reason. also prefer a short toggle for "auto-rollback on error rate" in the modal. backend already supports a 5-min window for rollback triggers.
aria_a11y: microcopy tweak for screen readers: start modal with an H1 that reads exactly: "Confirm canary rollout" and the confirm button should say "Confirm: route 50% to v2-alpha" (explicit action). avoid ambiguous labels like "Proceed".
laura.design: thanks. on timeline density — two options: (A) compact mini-scrubber that shows stacked traffic bands for each version (higher density, less text), or (B) expanded timeline with 1 row per version + clear labels. pros/cons: A saves space and makes comparisons easier; B is more legible and better for accessibility. thoughts?
sophia_research: users preferred B for auditability. they liked seeing a vertical ruler + timestamps when scanning history. A was faster for glanceable comparisons but caused mis-clicks in tests.
mike.eng: performance note — mini-scrubber with many versions increases DOM and charting cost. we can virtualize beyond N versions, or collapse older history into an aggregated bucket.
ben_pm: product preference: default to B for accessibility, with an option to toggle to compact. require keyboard shortcut to expand/compress.
laura.design: ok — default expanded timeline with a compact toggle. I'll mock updates for the modal copy and timeline control. one last copy ask: what should the speedbump CTA read? choices: "Confirm rollout", "Start canary", "Increase to 50%".
aria_a11y: "Increase to 50%" is best — it's explicit and includes the target. ensure button text includes the numeric percent.
ben_pm: +1. also add a small inline note under CTA: "This change is immediate; alerts will be sent to #deployments and on-call."
mike.eng: implementation question — if we require typing variant name for >50% do we lock out API calls? curious about auth surface. i think lock should apply to both UI and API key paths (rate-limited).
laura.design: good point — will propose calling out API restrictions in docs.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started by ben_pm — v2-alpha at 50% (auto-rollback=false) — 2025-04-03T10:15:00Z
laura.design: thanks all — I'll push a new figma with updated modal copy, accessibility notes, and timeline default. ping me if you want to be on a short review session tomorrow. :sparkles:
